source_text: Quoniam ex imparibus bonis compositi sumus, animum corpori debere dominari: quorum alterum nobis cum diis, alterum cum belluis commemoras esse commune. Et ideo id quod est melius, id est, animum virtute praeditum - dicis - et membris corporis bene et cupiditatibus imperare?
pass_a_gloss: Quoniam from unequal goods compositi sumus, animum to-the-body to-owe dominari: quorum the-other to-us when/with diis, the-other when/with belluis commemoras to-be commune. and for-that-reason it that/which is melius, it is, animum by-virtue praeditum - you-say - and members of-the-body well and cupiditatibus imperare?
pass_b_english: Since we are composed of unequal goods, the soul ought to rule the body. We share the one with the gods and the other with beasts. Therefore the better part—the soul endowed with virtue—rightly commands both the body’s members and its desires.

choices.why: Image of God in the soul; keep soul not 'mind' or 'life-force'.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded. Julian is not first-English.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Contra Iulianum / Against Julian), including authorities Julian quoted; Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
